changed.headline: Because of an AI voice assistant, Dane County officials say more than 24,000 non-emergency calls were handled in its first month, freeing dispatchers for 911.
Because of an AI call service, the San Diego County Sheriff's Office says it answers up to 20% of non-emergency calls without a dispatcher.
Because of an AI call assistant, Sparks Police in Nevada says it answered 25% of its non-emergency calls in the system's first two weeks.

Because of autonomous AI diabetic eye screening in Johns Hopkins primary care, African-American patients were more likely to present to specialist eye care, an exploratory association (p = 0.02).
Because of AI tools in its National TB Elimination Programme, India's government says adverse TB outcomes fell 27%.

Because of AI chest X-ray tools in half of England's NHS trusts, the government says scans are analysed in an average of 4 days instead of 8 for the most complex cases, and more than 4 million patients have had a faster lung cancer diagnosis or all-clear.

Because of AI, 189 patients on chemotherapy in Qingdao who got a nurse-supervised AI follow-up system reported quality of life 5.88 points higher than patients on conventional follow-up.

The report supports a government-reported 27% decline after nationwide deployment, without an independent evaluation or isolated AI effect. Its table attributes the 4,500-plus alerts to Media Disease Surveillance, rather than the TB programme.

The complete press release supports the reported 4 versus 8 days and more than 4 million patients as government claims. It provides neither a measurement period nor an independent evaluation isolating AI's contribution.
